faq.a: Tahsin is associated with the Arabic form تَحْسِين, whose core sense is tahsin; improvement, beautification.

faq.q: What is the origin of Tahsin?
faq.a: Tahsin is associated with Arabic. Tahsin is Arabic تَحْسِين (Taḥsīn), the verbal noun of حَسَّنَ, meaning 'improvement, beautification'.
Yes — the underlying form تَحْسِين is Arabic.
Tahsin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Tahsin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ح س ن is Quranic, but Taḥsīn is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Tahsin mean in Persian?

A romanized syllable approximation is tah-sin. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Tahsin?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Tahsin, tahsin. Script forms are تحسین, تَحْسِين, तहसीन.

faq.q: Is Tahsin a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
